day.eyebrow: How it is used · an ordinary day
day.title: A day with AdelIA
day.intro: Adel is 13 months old and has just started daycare. This is what Adel's mother does with AdelIA on an ordinary day.
day.s1Lead: A voice note on Telegram, saved in the diary with the date.
day.s1Snippet: Slept through the night, two feeds and a bit of a runny nose, no fever.
day.s2Lead: One photo and AdelIA pulls out each data point, dated.
day.s3Title: Visit to the pediatrician, recorded with her consent
day.s3Lead: A two-voice transcript and the key points.
day.s3B2: Paracetamol if she goes above 38 °C, at the dose for her weight.
day.s3B4: If no better in 48 hours, come back.
day.s4Lead: Ask the record, the clinical guidelines and the studies. It answers with citations.
day.s4Q: Is it normal for a 13-month-old to want only breast milk?
day.s4A: At 13 months, preferring only breast milk can be normal during stress or adaptation, since breastfeeding is still nutritious and gives emotional security without compromising nutrition if feeds are frequent [ev_1].
day.s4Src1: ev_1 · Mi bebé empieza la guardería, ¿cómo puedo mantener la lactancia materna? · Familia y Salud (AEPap), 2022
day.s5Lead: One page on the week, citing the record and the evidence.
day.s5R1: Fever of 38.2 on Friday, paracetamol prescribed [1]. Eating less and asking for the breast, mostly since starting daycare [2].
day.s5R2: Seeking the breast during adaptation does not compromise nutrition [ev_1].
day.s5R3: Should we check weight again in two weeks?
day.footnote: Illustrative examples built with AdelIA's real features. Adel's data is not real.
day.disclaimer: This day is an example, and AdelIA does not replace medical advice. What the pediatrician says here about fever and paracetamol is for Adel, not for your baby: the dose and what to do are for your own pediatrician to decide. In an emergency, call 112.

home.proofQuestion: Is it normal for my baby to spit up after every feed?
home.proofAnswer: Regurgitation is common in infants and usually resolves by 12 months without treatment; red flags are weight loss, feed refusal or blood.
home.feature1Body: Every report on your baby, encrypted in a private vault. You decide what's shared, and with whom.
home.feature2Body: No vague answers: every interpretation is backed by clinical guidelines and pediatric studies, cited and verifiable.
home.feature3Body: A clear summary for the visit. The pediatrician gets the picture in 30 seconds.

home.modeADemoQ: When should I worry about spit-up?
home.modeADemoA: Red flags are weight loss, food refusal or blood; without them it's usually physiological and improves by the first year.
home.modeBDemoS1: Mild physiological reflux, improving. Vaccines up to date.
home.modeBDemoS2: Weight and height curve within expected percentiles.
home.modeBDemoS3: Should we review the introduction of solid foods?
home.evTitle: The answers you just saw have sources.
home.evBody: To answer you, AdelIA searches its library of clinical guidelines, studies and pages from pediatric associations. Each answer shows the sources it used so you can read them. If it cannot find enough evidence, it prefers not to answer.
home.vsTitle: Same question. Two very different answers.
home.vsQuestion: “Is it safe to give my baby an antacid for reflux?”
home.vsGptAnswer: Antacids can generally be used in babies, but you should check with your pediatrician. Every case is different and there are several options.
home.vsGptNote: No source. Doesn't know your baby. Sounds safe even when it's wrong.
home.vsAdeliaAnswer: The evidence does not support routine acid suppression for regurgitation in healthy infants; it's reserved for confirmed reflux disease.
home.vsAdeliaNote: Backed by a specific, cited, verifiable study. And cross-checked with your baby's history.
home.vsR1L: Cites the study it comes from
home.vsR2A: Yes: guideline title, organization and year, with a link
home.vsR3A: Yes: searches their reports, lab results and recorded visits

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: At AdelIA we keep your baby's health history so you always have it on hand, with help from AI. Here's what data we keep, where it's processed, and what rights you have, in plain language.
privacy.whatBody: Your account (the email we use for your passwordless magic-link sign-in), your baby's profiles (name, date of birth, sex, your relationship to them), the documents you upload (PDF reports, photos, or audio), the text and clinical data our AI extracts from them, your chat history with the assistant, the briefings you generate, the consent events logged for each recording, and your subscription status. All of it exists for one purpose: building your baby's health history and helping you understand it. Legal basis: performance of our contract with you, and for your baby's health data, your explicit consent as the holder of parental authority (GDPR Art. 9.2.a).
privacy.whereTitle: Where it's processed, and who else touches it
privacy.whereBody: Our servers are our own, based in Spain. Current processors: Mistral AI (France) handles documents, text, and audio (OCR, embeddings, chat, transcription), all within the EU. Stripe processes your subscription payment. Resend sends the email with your access link. Cloudflare (Cloudflare, Inc., USA) terminates the TLS encryption for adelia.godi.ai, acts as the content delivery network and provides the access tunnel that brings visits to our server. That means all traffic between your browser and AdelIA, health data included, passes through its network, which is global and can route it through data centers outside the EU. The transfer rests on Cloudflare's certification under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework and, as a fallback, on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses in its data processing addendum. If you choose the optional Telegram diary, your messages and voice notes travel through Telegram's servers (Telegram FZ-LLC, Dubai) like any chat in that app; our server downloads them, stores them in Spain, and transcription still runs on Mistral (EU). Telegram only keeps the conversation you can see, which you can delete from the app itself. Nothing goes further than these five. We may switch transcription providers in the future (for example, to another EU-based service); if we do, we'll let you know. We don't use third-party analytics or tracking tools: no Google Analytics, no pixels, no advertising cookies (all we count is four aggregate numbers on our own server, explained further down). We set only two technical cookies: the session one that keeps you signed in, and one that remembers the language you pick.
privacy.retentionBody: As long as your account exists, we keep your data so your baby's history stays available. The one exception is consultation audio: it's deleted automatically once it's transcribed, within 48 hours at most (7 days if transcription fails). An automated check runs every hour, so nothing sits around waiting. If you delete your account, everything cascades away with it: profiles, documents, extracted text, briefings, and conversations.
privacy.recordingsBody: When you record a consultation, the app requires you to announce it first: you can only start recording once you confirm the healthcare professional knows. Nothing is ever recorded secretly. The audio uploads encrypted, gets transcribed into text inside your baby's private history, and is then deleted (see 'How long we keep it'). That transcript may include the professional's own words, personal data of theirs that we process on the basis of our legitimate interest in documenting the consultation for your baby's care, weighed against their right to privacy. The professional can object at any time: they can ask you to discard the recording (there's a button for that) or write directly to security@godi.ai. Recordings are for your personal, family use only. Publishing, broadcasting, or sharing them outside that use is not allowed (we cover this in the terms of use too).
privacy.rightsTitle: Your rights, and how to use them
privacy.rightsBody: Access: all your data is visible inside the app, any time. Rectification: you can correct profiles and details from your account. Erasure: you can delete your entire account, and everything in it, from settings (you can also delete a single document from its own page, and download all your data in one click from Settings, with the clinical core in FHIR format). Objection: a recorded professional can object to how we process their voice. To exercise any of these rights, or for any other question, write to security@godi.ai. If you're not satisfied, you can file a complaint with the AEPD in Spain or the CNIL in France.
privacy.neverBody: We never sell your data or your baby's, to anyone, ever. We don't use your information to train AI models. We don't track you: there is no third-party analytics and no advertising in AdelIA, and the aggregate counters we do keep cannot say who you are or whether you came back. AdelIA is open-source software (AGPL-3.0); if you'd rather host it yourself, you can, and in that case whoever runs the deployment is responsible for that data, not Godi.AI.
privacy.contactBody: Data controller: Godi.AI (Santiago Patiño Serna). For any question, or to exercise your rights: security@godi.ai.
privacy.metaDescription: What data AdelIA keeps about your baby, where it is processed (EU), for how long and what your rights are: export, correct or delete everything in one click.
privacy.countersBody: To find out whether AdelIA is any use to anyone, we count four numbers a day on our own server: how many times a public page was viewed, how many times “Get started” was pressed, how many accounts were created, and how many reached the dashboard. That is literally all it is: a date, an event name and an integer that goes up by one. We store no IP, no browser, no referrer and no identifier, and we set and read no cookie to count it. Two people and one person twice are the same “2”, so not even we can tell whether you came back. These numbers never leave our server and only the person running AdelIA reads them. Legal basis: our legitimate interest in knowing whether the product is used, with no impact on you because none of the count is about you.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.intro: These are AdelIA's terms of use. We wrote them in plain language because we want you to actually read them, not just click accept. Questions go to security@godi.ai.
terms.whatBody: AdelIA is a tool for keeping your baby's health history and making it easier to understand, with help from AI. It is not a medical device and carries no MDR certification, and it doesn't replace the advice, diagnosis, or treatment of a healthcare professional. Whenever you have a question about your baby's health, always ask a professional.
terms.accountBody: You sign in with your email through a magic link: no passwords to remember or leak. You're responsible for keeping access to that inbox secure. You can use AdelIA for your children's health data if you're their parent or legal guardian, with your explicit consent, as the holder of parental authority.
terms.trialBody: AdelIA’s Managed plan includes a 30-day free trial without a card. If you choose to subscribe, Stripe will ask for a card and the subscription will cost €8/month. Any remaining trial days are honoured before the first charge. Without a subscription, access to paid features is restricted when the trial ends; there is no automatic charge. You can cancel your subscription from billing. You can also self-host the open-source software at no licence cost.
terms.useBody: AdelIA is for your personal, family use: documenting your baby's health. On consultation recordings, the rule is simple: you can only record if you announce it to the professional beforehand, and the app requires you to confirm that. Never record secretly. That recording is for your private history; publishing it, posting it, or sharing it with anyone outside your personal use is not allowed. You also can't use AdelIA to upload documents that aren't yours or your children's, or for anything that breaks the law or infringes on someone else's rights.
terms.dataTitle: Your data is yours, and the software is free
terms.dataBody: Everything you upload, and everything the AI generates from it, belongs to you. We don't sell it or use it to train models. AdelIA's code is open, under the AGPL-3.0 license: you can read it, audit it, or host it yourself on your own server. If you self-host, you become responsible for that data, not Godi.AI.
terms.liabilityBody: AdelIA is provided 'as is'. We work hard to keep transcriptions and document summaries reliable, but AI can make mistakes: always double-check anything important, and don't make health decisions based solely on what the app tells you. To the extent the law allows, Godi.AI isn't liable for indirect damages arising from your use of the service. Nothing here limits the rights the law grants you as a consumer.
terms.lawBody: These terms are governed by Spanish law. For any question, complaint, or to exercise your data rights, write to security@godi.ai first; we'll try to resolve it within a reasonable time. For data-protection complaints specifically, you can turn to the AEPD in Spain or the CNIL in France.
